finding.summary: Success-record polling is not operation drainage and can replace the original failure.

finding.productionBoundaryReviewed: backend/common/services/mongoTransaction.js awaits session.endSession() in finally before its returned promise settles.
finding.minimalRecommendation: Release the barrier, await settlement of all tracked full execute/transaction promises, restore patched methods reliably, and preserve both body and execution errors. Do not require a succeeded command row as cleanup evidence.

limits: This diagnostic demonstrates JavaScript cleanup control flow with substitutes, not an observed production data-loss or authorization bug.

provenance.reviewAndDiagnosticSource: Actual source reads, node --check results, and independent Node diagnostic output in the preceding helper-review turn of this chat
provenance.description: This is a retrospective record of the independent helper review and diagnostic execution, plus a separate read-only check of the developer browser r4 log. It is not a Jest JSON report or an independent browser execution report.

review.previousP2Disposition: Implementation fixed; independent reviewer recommends closing the cleanup finding, not automatically closing the entire final-integration gate.

checks.conclusion: Calls are registered on entry to execute, before the insert barrier; synchronous throws become tracked rejections, and rejection handling is attached immediately.

Cleanup closes admission, releases the barrier, awaits all registered outcome promises without rejection short-circuiting, and restores both methods afterward. Distinct body and execution failures are retained in AggregateError.
The full transaction runner promise includes commit or rollback and awaited endSession cleanup.
The wrapper receives the formal recurring service object from the Express request listener app.locals. Production routes dynamically access service.execute, so the wrapper is on the request path.
The comment now accurately describes persistent recovery after document replacement, late commit and lost response; it no longer claims an old-document success-callback epoch test.
The three permanent cases cover rollback cleanup, combined body and pre-insert failure, and success cleanup. They use control-flow substitutes, not real HTTP or MongoDB rollback injection.

independentNodeDiagnostics.method: Loaded the actual recurringBarrier helper in a standalone Node process with node:assert/strict. Used synthetic service and Command objects, deferred cleanup promises, and setImmediate turns to check non-settlement and restoration order.
independentNodeDiagnostics.countingNote: The closing-admission check was executed inside the multiple-call diagnostic and shared its output line. Four assertion groups are not four processes, four Jest cases, or four browser cases.

assertions: Tracked one insert-path rollback and one pre-insert failure while the body also failed.

An execute call during cleanup rejected with the barrier-is-closing error.
The original execute call count remained two; the rejected call did not enter business execution.
A synchronous throw from original execute was propagated as the identical original error object.
A successful insert did not settle the helper while deferred execution cleanup remained pending.
After cleanup was released, the helper returned the body result and restored both original methods.
